BURHAN:v2p129/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.claim: The Prophet supported his descriptions of Paradise with verses: unseen delights by 32:17, the promise to work by the verses of al-Layl, and the tree's long shade by 56:30.
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.anchor: منها حين ذكر ما أعد الله تعالى لأوليائه فى الجنة فقال فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر

QASHANI:92:2-6/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:2-6/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:2-6/r5.claim: The good and highest state is the rank of perfection, affirmed through certain intellectual faith; without confidence in perfection, spiritual ascent is impossible.
QASHANI:92:2-6/r5.anchor: التي هي مرتبة الكمال بالإيمان العلمي إذ لو لم يتيقن بوجود كمال كامل

QASHANI:92:2-6/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:2-6/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:2-6/r6.claim: Making the easy way easy means preparing and assisting the seeker in God’s path by cutting attachments and strengthening certainty.
QASHANI:92:2-6/r6.anchor: أي فسنهيئه ونوفقه للطريقة اليسرى التي هي السلوك في الله

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.claim: Verses 5–7 describe the character and belief that qualify a person for success in the Hereafter and ease the way to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.anchor: Mentioned in these verses are the character and ideology which entitles a person to the successes of the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r1.claim: In al-ḥusnā, an omitted noun such as al-ʿāqibah (fate or outcome) is understood: the virtuous believe spending and goodness will bring good results.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r1.anchor: The implication is that they have faith that spending in the way of God and virtue will reap good results for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.claim: Fear of the Hereafter and belief in reward motivate virtue; without such faith, a person lacks an urge to give or gives for worldly benefit, without divine blessing, as 107:1–3 illustrates.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.anchor: will be rewarded in the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.claim: The virtuous fight their base desires at every step and grow stronger through that struggle, eventually reaching the servants’ company and Paradise described at 89:29–30.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.anchor: gradually gain the strength needed to fight

QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r7.claim: The good promise may mean Paradise, the final world, forgiveness of grave sinners, the Prophet's intercession, or God's compensation.
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r7.anchor: بالجنة ، أو بالكرة الآخرة ، وبالمغفرة لأهل الكبائر

SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.claim: The generous give up both abodes while seeking God's pleasure, avoid frivolity and doubtful matters, and persist in seeking nearness.
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أعطى الدارين ، ولم يرهما شيئا في طلب رضا الله واتقى اللغو ، والشبهات وصدق بالحسنى

SULAMI:v2p398#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r2.claim: The promise of what is good is interpreted as gnosis.

SULAMI:v2p398#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r3.claim: What is good means well-being in this world and forgiveness in the next.
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : العافية في الدنيا ، والمغفرة في العقبى

TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.claim: Abu Bakr gave his utmost from himself and wealth, avoided settling into the natural self, and affirmed the good promise as the word of monotheism.
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.anchor: أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أعطى من نفسه وماله مجهوده، واتقى سكونه

TUSTARI:92:5-6/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r2.speaker: قيل
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r2.claim: An unnamed interpretation identifies al-husna with the reward.

TUSTARI:92:5-6/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r3.speaker: ويقال
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r3.claim: Another unnamed interpretation identifies al-husna with sincerity.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها ، ذكر هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and others understand al-ḥusnā as affirming God's promise made in this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r14.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة: هي الحلف في الدنيا الوارد به وعد الله تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r15.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r15.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and others understand al-ḥusnā as Paradise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r16.claim: Other interpretations identify al-ḥusnā as reward or as the confession lā ilāha illā Allāh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r16.anchor: وقال جماعة: الثواب. وقال السلمي وغيره: لا إله إلا الله.

FARRA:v3p270/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p270/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p270/r4.claim: Abū Bakr spent his own money to buy nine enslaved men from polytheists seeking God, and he is the one who gave, feared God, and affirmed the good promise.
FARRA:v3p270/r4.anchor: اشترى تسعة رجال كانوا في أيدي المشركين من ماله يريد به الله تبارك وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r1.claim: Al-Sulami and others, and in a report from Ibn Abbas, take al-husna as the statement “there is no god but God”; another view includes any truth-bearing word.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r1.anchor: وصدق بالحسنى أي بالكلمة الحسنى وهي كما قال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة وجماعة وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r2.claim: Ikrima and a group, also reported from Ibn Abbas, take al-husna as the good religion of Islam.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r2.anchor: أو بالملة الحسنى وهي ملة الإسلام وقال عكرمة وجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies al-husna as Paradise; another view takes it as recompense in general.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد الجنة وقيل المثوبة مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r4.claim: Alusi prefers a comprehensive reading: giving signifies worship, taqwa includes all good actions and avoiding sins, and belief in al-husna means faith in tawhid and all required beliefs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r4.anchor: ويترجح عندي أن الإعطاء إشارة إلى العبادة والأتقاء إشارة إلى ما يشمل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.speaker: أبو قحافة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.claim: A report authenticated by al-Hakim says Abu Quhafa questioned Abu Bakr for freeing weak slaves instead of strong men who could protect him; Abu Bakr said he acted for God's sake, and the verses were revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.anchor: عن عامر بن عبد الله ابن الزبير عن أبيه قال قال أبو قحافة لأبي بكر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf; the surah's opening verses were then revealed. A similar occasion is related for Abu al-Dahdah.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال أن أبا بكر اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.claim: Mentioning belief after taqwa singles out the specific after the general and maintains the rhyme; another suggestion is that listening to learn monotheism is part of giving obedience and avoiding shirk part of taqwa, but Alusi rejects it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.anchor: ولما كان الإيمان أمرا معتنى به في نفسه أخر عن الأتقاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r7.claim: They, with an account from Ibn Abbas, interpret الحسنى as affirming ‘there is no god but God.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك: وصدق بلا إله إلا الله، وهي رواية عطية عن ابن عباس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says الحسنى is Paradise, citing the promise that those who do good receive the best.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بالجنة دليله: قوله تعالى "للذين أحسنوا الحسنى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r9.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas’s interpretation: believing in the promised replacement, that God will compensate the giver.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: "صدق بالحسنى": أي بالخلف، أي أيقن أن الله تعالى سيخلفه. وهي رواية عكرمة عن ابن عباس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r10.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r10.claim: They understand الحسنى as God’s promise to reward the giver.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي: بموعود الله عز وجل الذي وعده أن يثيبه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.claim: In this story, the giver is Abu al-Dahdah, the promised good is reward, and the easier path is Paradise; the miser is the Ansari, who denies reward and is eased toward Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.anchor: {وأما من بخل واستغنى} يعني الأنصاري، {وكذب بالحسنى} يعني الثواب، {فسنيسره للعسرى} يعني النار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.claim: The fortunate person gives obedience, avoids sin, and believes the true, good promise, including the declaration of God’s oneness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى } تفصيل مبين لتشتت المساعي

BINTSHATI:v2p105/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r2.claim: Husn means beauty and is used materially against ugliness and morally against evil; husna is a feminine superlative for the utmost good, opposed to saw'a.
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r2.anchor: والحسن في اللغة الجمال، ويغلب استعماله في الماديات

BINTSHATI:v2p105/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r3.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r3.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes husn, used for objects and events, hasana, which as a noun is used for events, and husna, used only for events.
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r3.anchor: وفرق الراغب فب (المفردات) بين الحسن والحسنة والحسنى

BINTSHATI:v2p105/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r4.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r4.claim: Exegetes interpret al-husna as a good outcome, belief in God's oneness, or confidence that God will repay the spender; the author says good outcome can encompass all three.
BINTSHATI:v2p105/r4.anchor: وقد تأول المفسرون الحسنى بحسن العاقبة، وبالإيمان بوحدانية الله

BINTSHATI:v2p107/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r4.claim: Truthfulness can describe words, deeds, intention, and belief; Quranic affirmation most often means believing in God, His signs, messengers, words, and meeting Him.
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r4.anchor: وأكثر ما يكون التصديق في القرآن الكريم بمعناه الديني في التصديق بالله

BINTSHATI:v2p107/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r5.claim: The author keeps al-husna broad enough to include the interpretations of reward in this life and the next, Paradise, recompense, and monotheism.
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r5.anchor: وإن كان الأولى إطلاقها لتعم فلا تختص بوجه من هذه الوجوه

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.claim: The giver gives what God prescribed and commanded, while the God-fearing person protects himself through obedience and avoiding sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } أي وقع منه إعطاء على ما حددنا له وأمرناه به { واتقى * }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r2.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the excellent word of justice: monotheism and its related promises about the afterlife, worldly provision, and Islam’s triumph.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r2.anchor: وهي كلمة العدل التي هي أحسن الكلام من التوحيد وما يتفرع عنه من الوعود الصادقة بالآخرة

NAHHAS:v5p241/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r8.claim: Basri grammarians parse man as the subject; Kufans parse the resumptive pronoun attached to the following verb as its syntactic support.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r8.anchor: من في موضع رفع بالابتداء عند البصريين وعند الكوفيين بالهاء العائدة عليه

NAHHAS:v5p241/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p241/r10.claim: He interprets affirming al-ḥusnā as affirming the oath; the source calls the chain reliable and the reading suited to context.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس وصدق بالحسنى قال بالحلف فهذا إسناد مستقيم ومعنى ملائم لسياق الكلام

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.claim: He reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal for God; the verses contrast their efforts with those of Umayya and Ubayy, identify the good as the testimony of faith, and the hard path as Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن عساكر عن ابن مسعود

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.claim: Giving means giving from one's bounty and fearing God; the good promise is God's compensation, ease is good, and the opposite is withholding wealth, self-sufficiency, denial, and ease toward evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.claim: He said the giver pays God's due, avoids prohibitions, and believes God's promise; the miser withholds that due, feels self-sufficient, and denies the promise.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r8.claim: He glossed affirming the good as certainty in God's compensation.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.claim: He also glossed the good as affirming that there is no god but God; the miser is one who withholds zakat despite having been enriched.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r10.claim: He glossed al-husna as ‘there is no god but God.’
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r10.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r1.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.claim: Abu Bakr freed weak women who accepted Islam; when his father urged him to free strong protectors instead, he replied that he sought God's reward, and a family member said these verses were revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن عساكر عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.claim: The Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Fire is written, but commanded people to act: each is made ready for the deeds of the saved or the wretched, then recited this passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وعبد بن حميد والبخاري ومسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجة وابن مردويه وابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.claim: Suraqa asked whether deeds were predetermined; the Prophet affirmed the decree but urged action, since each person is eased toward what he was created for, then recited the passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد ومسلم وابن حبان والطبراني وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.speaker: بشير بن كعب الأسلمي
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.claim: Asked about deeds, he reports the Prophet answering that they follow the written decree, yet people must act because each is eased toward what he was created for; he recited these verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن قانع وابن شاهين وعبدان كلهم في الصحابة عن بشير بن كعب الأسلمي

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.claim: Abu Qahafa urged freeing strong men who could protect Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr said he sought God's face, and the report says the passage through ‘he will be satisfied’ was revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the sura's revelation to a sale: a stingy palm owner deprived a poor household of fallen dates, then a believer traded forty palms for the tree and gave it to the family; the buyer received a promised palm in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان رجلا كان له نخل ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the giver fears his Lord, believes in God's promised recompense, and is eased toward good by God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : فاما من اعطى من الفضل واتقى قال : اتقى ربه وصدق بالحسنى قال : صدق بالخلق من الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r4.claim: Qatadah says believing in the good means trusting God's promise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r4.anchor: وصدق بالحسنى قال : بموعود الله على نفسه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r7.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says the good promised is Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r7.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الحسنى قال : الحسنى : الجن

IBNASHUR:92:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:6/r1.claim: Al-husna is the feminine of al-ahsan and originally an adjective with an omitted feminine noun, potentially reward, victory, promise, or outcome.
IBNASHUR:92:6/r1.anchor: تأنيث الأحسن فهي بالأصالة صفة لموصوف مقدر

IBNASHUR:92:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:6/r2.anchor: وقد يصير هذا الوصف علما بالغلبة فقيل :  الحسنى الجنة

IBNASHUR:92:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:6/r3.claim: Some identify al-husna as the testimony of faith.
IBNASHUR:92:6/r3.anchor: فقيل :  الحسنى الجنة ، وقيل :  كلمة الشهادة

IBNASHUR:92:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:6/r6.claim: Across these readings, affirming it means acknowledging its occurrence and implies wanting to attain it; the possibilities ultimately concern faith in God's promise of good reward, victory, or compensation.
IBNASHUR:92:6/r6.anchor: وعلى الوجوه كلها فالتصديق بها الاعتراف بوقوعها ويكنى به عن الرغبة في تحصيلها

IBNASHUR:92:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:6/r7.claim: Belief in al-husna entails doing the deeds by which success is attained, and contrasts with the denial in verse 9.
IBNASHUR:92:6/r7.anchor: ويتضمن أنه يعمل الأعمال التي يحصل بها الفوز بالحسنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r7.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and others say al-husna means there is no god but God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r7.anchor: فقال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وغيره: هي لا إله إلا الله،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and others identify it as God's promised compensation, illustrated by the angels' prayer for spender and miser.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة: هي الخلف الذي وعد الله تعالى به،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r9.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وجماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r9.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and others say al-husna means Paradise.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r10.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r10.claim: Many commentators interpret al-husna generally as reward and recompense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r10.anchor: وقال كثير من المفسرين «الحسنى» : الأجر والثواب مجملا.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r9.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطية، الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r9.claim: Al-ḥusnā means the declaration that there is no god but God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r9.anchor: أنه لا إله إلا الله رواه عطية عن ابن عباس وبه قال الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r10.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة، الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r10.claim: Al-ḥusnā means the promised recompense or return.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r10.anchor: الخلف رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس وبه قال الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r12.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r12.claim: Al-ḥusnā means God's blessings upon a person.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r13.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r13.claim: Al-ḥusnā means God's promise to reward the person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r13.anchor: بوعد الله أن يثيبه قاله قتادة ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r14.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r14.claim: Al-ḥusnā means prayer, zakat, and fasting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r14.anchor: الصلاة والزكاة والصوم قاله زيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r2.claim: Qatadah interprets the good promise as recompense, and Khasif as reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r2.anchor: أي: بالمجازاة على ذلك -قاله قتادة، وقال خصيف: بالثواب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Salih, and Zayd ibn Aslam take the good promise as God's compensation or replacement for what is given.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وأبو صالح، وزيد بن أسلم: {وصدق بالحسنى} أي: بالخلف.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r4.claim: Abu al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Dahhak say the good promise is the testimony that there is no god but God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي، والضحاك: {وصدق بالحسنى} أي: بلا إله إلا الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r5.claim: In another report, Ikrimah interprets the good promise as what God has bestowed on a person.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r5.anchor: وفي رواية عن عكرمة: {وصدق بالحسنى} أي: بما أنعم الله عليه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam also interprets it as prayer, alms, and fasting, and in another statement as the obligatory end-of-Ramadan charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r6.anchor: وفي رواية عن زيد بن أسلم: {وصدق بالحسنى} قال: الصلاة والزكاة والصوم. وقال مرة: وصدقة الفطر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r7.claim: The Prophet identifies the good promise as Paradise in a report from Ubayy ibn Ka'b.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r7.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الحسنى قال: "الحسنى: الجنة"

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r6.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form of “best” and refers to the supreme blessing because of its excellent outcome.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r6.anchor: والحسنى: تأنيث الأحسن، وهي النعمة العظمى لحسن موقعها

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.claim: The passage begins its account of three reported occasions for revelation with Abū Bakr; the next part continues those reports.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.anchor: أولها: أنها نزلت في أبي بكر

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r1.claim: The preceding occasion report identifies Abū Bakr; this segment continues the source's differing accounts and argues that the passage's point is general.

KASHSHAF:92:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:6/r1.claim: Al-ḥusnā may mean the good quality of faith, the good religion of Islam, or the good reward of Paradise.
KASHSHAF:92:6/r1.anchor: بالخصلة الحسنى : وهي الإيمان . أو بالملة الحسنى : وهي ملة الإسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r2.claim: We will ease him toward ease means preparing him for it, as a horse is saddled and bridled, and guiding him until obedience becomes easy; compare the promise to open one's heart to Islam.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r2.anchor: فسنهيؤه لها من يسر الفرس للركوب إذا أسرجها وألجمها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says each person is facilitated toward the purpose for which he was created.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r19.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r19.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets al-husna as God's oneness, expressed by there being no god but God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r19.anchor: بتوحيد الله , وهو قول لا إله إلا الله , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r20.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r20.claim: Qatada takes al-husna to mean God's promise.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r23.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r23.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets it as prayer, alms, and fasting.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r23.anchor: بالصلاة والزكاة والصوم , قاله زيد بن أسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r24.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r24.claim: Ata says it means what God has bestowed on the person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r24.anchor: السادس : بما أنعم الله عليه , قاله عطاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r25.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r25.claim: Al-Hasan takes it as confidence that God will replace what one gives; Mawardi says most of these readings are close in meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r25.anchor: السابع : بالخلف من عطائه , قاله الحسن , ومعاني أكثرها متقاربة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.speaker: أبو الدرداء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.claim: Qatada reports from Khulayd, from Abu al-Darda, that the Prophet said two angels call each sunrise for God to replace the spender's gift and ruin the hoarder's wealth, then recited these verses; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.anchor: يروي قتادة عن خليد عن أبي الدرداء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من يوم طلعت فيه شمسه إلا وملكان يناديان : اللهم

MUJAHID:v2p765/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p765/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p765/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person affirms God's replacement or compensation for what was given.
MUJAHID:v2p765/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ﴿ وصدق بالحسنى ﴾ قال يقول صدق بالخلف

MUQATIL:92:2-6/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:92:2-6/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:92:2-6/r6.claim: Abu Bakr answered that he hoped for forgiveness and promised to remind Abu Sufyan on the day he entered Saqar; Abu Sufyan mocked belief in resurrection and insisted the spent wealth was lost.
MUQATIL:92:2-6/r6.anchor: قال أبو بكر، رضي الله عنه: والله، لأذكرنك هذا اليوم يا أبا سفيان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r1.claim: Al-husna may mean the beautiful religion of Islam.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r1.anchor: ملة الحسنى وهى ملة الاسلام أو بالمثوبة الحسنى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r2.claim: Al-husna may mean the beautiful reward, Paradise.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r2.anchor: بالمثوبة الحسنى وهى الحنة أو بالكلمة وهى لا إله إلا الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r3.claim: Al-husna may mean the testimony 'There is no god but God.'
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#7/r3.anchor: أو بالكلمة وهى لا إله إلا الله

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r4.claim: Believing in al-ḥusnā means trusting God's replacement reward for what one gives.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r4.anchor: { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالخلف من الله تعالى على عطائه.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r10.speaker: الضحاك والسلمي وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r10.claim: They gloss al-ḥusnā as the testimony that there is no god but God.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r11.claim: He says it means Paradise, supported by 10:26.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بالجنة دليله قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r12.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r12.claim: He says it is God's promise to reward the believer.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r12.anchor: بموعود الله الذي وعده أن يثيبه

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r13.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r13.claim: He identifies al-ḥusnā as prayer, almsgiving, and fasting.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r14.speaker: الحسن والطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r14.claim: Hasan interprets it as God's compensation for giving, and al-Tabari chooses this view; the author says all explanations converge on reward and Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r14.anchor: الحسن: بالخلف من عطائه وهو اختيار الطبري. وتقدم عن ابن عباس، وكله متقارب المعنى إذ كله يرجع إلى الثواب

QUTB-ZILAL:92:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:6/r1.claim: Al-husna is the name and identifying designation of the creed.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:6/r2.claim: Giving, piety, and affirmation represent the person’s utmost effort to purify and guide the self, meriting God’s freely willed aid and success, without which nothing is possible.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:6/r2.anchor: والذي يعطي ويتقي ويصدق بالحسنى يكون قد بذل أقصى ما في وسعه ليزكي نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.claim: The passage explains that the differing human paths end in praiseworthy or blameworthy outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.anchor: بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة والمذمومة

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r4.claim: One meaning of al-husna is the testimony of God's unity, encompassing tawhid and prophethood; giving and restraint alone do not benefit without faith, as in 90:14-17.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r4.anchor: أنها قول لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r5.claim: Another meaning is belief in the goodness of God's prescribed bodily and financial laws.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r5.anchor: أن الحسنى عبارة عما فرضه الله تعالى من العبادات على الأبدان

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r6.claim: A third meaning is confidence that God will replace what is spent, as promised in 34:39 and illustrated by 2:261; denying this promise reflects bad opinion of God.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r6.anchor: أن الحسنى هو الخلف الذي وعده الله في قوله : { وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه }

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that two angels call daily for God to replace the spender's wealth and destroy the miser's.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r7.anchor: وروي عن أبي الدرداء أنه قال : ( ما من يوم غربت فيه الشمس

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r8.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r8.claim: Al-Husna can mean reward or Paradise; Qatada says the person believes God's promise and acts for it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r8.anchor: قال قتادة : صدق بموعود الله فعمل لذلك الموعود

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r9.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r9.claim: Al-Qaffal says the word broadly includes every good quality, as in 9:52 and 42:23; increased reward is also called good in 42:23 and 41:50.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r9.anchor: قال القفال : وبالجملة أن الحسنى لفظة تسع كل خصلة حسنة

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet taught each person's destination is recorded, then urged action because everyone is eased toward what they were created for; he recited these verses.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.anchor: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib related that the Prophet said, “There is no one among you except that his place is registered

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.speaker: most
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.claim: Most take al-ḥusnā as the testimony that there is no god but God; another gloss is belief in God, either of which is attested to or denied.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.anchor: is taken by most to mean “There is no god but God” (Sh) or simply belief in God (Z)

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.claim: Others understand al-ḥusnā as Paradise, called the most beautiful reward in 3:148 and 3:195.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.anchor: others see it as a reference to Paradise, which is referred to as the most beautiful reward in 3:148 and 3:195

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.claim: Al-ḥusnā can also refer to God Himself, whose Most Beautiful Names are affirmed in several verses.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.anchor: it can also be seen as a reference to God Himself, for, as several verses attest, Unto Him belong the Most Beautiful Names

ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n3/r1.claim: The ultimate good is an absolute moral value independent of time and social circumstance, a moral imperative.
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n3/r1.anchor: in moral values independent of time and social circumstance and, hence, in the absolute

TAB:92:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:6/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, and Shahr b. Ḥawshab interpret the good promise as God's replacement for what the giver spends.
TAB:92:6/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  وَصَدّقَ بالْحُسْنَى قال :  وصدّق بالخَلَف من الله

TAB:92:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
TAB:92:6/r2.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān glosses the good promise as the confession that there is no god but God.
TAB:92:6/r2.anchor: عن أبي حصين ،   عن أبي عبد الرحمن وَصَدّقَ بالْحُسْنَى قال :  بلا إله إلاّ الله

TAB:92:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:92:6/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk likewise identifies it with the confession that there is no god but God.
TAB:92:6/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  وَصَدّقَ بالْحُسْنَى :  بلا إله إلاّ الله

TAB:92:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:6/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās also reads it as affirming that there is no god but God.
TAB:92:6/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس وَصَدّقَ بالْحُسْنَى :  يقول :  صدّق بلا إله إلاّ الله

TAB:92:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:92:6/r5.claim: Mujāhid interprets the good promise as Paradise.
TAB:92:6/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد وَصَدّقَ بالْحُسْنَى قال :  بالجنة

TAB:92:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:6/r6.claim: Qatāda says the believer affirms God's good promise and acts accordingly.
TAB:92:6/r6.anchor: عن قتادة وَصَدّقَ بالْحُسْنَى قال :  بموعود الله على نفسه ،   فعمل بذلك الموعود

TAB:92:6/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r7.speaker: author
TAB:92:6/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the promise of God's replacement for spending, since the passage first describes a spender seeking recompense and the Prophet's report supports this reading.
TAB:92:6/r7.anchor: وأشبه هذه الأقوال بما دلّ عليه ظاهر التنزيل ،   وأولاها بالصواب عندي :  قول من قال :  عُنِي به التصديق بالخَلَف من الله

TAB:92:6/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:92:6/r8.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports the Prophet's teaching that angels pray at each sunset for spenders to receive replacement and misers to suffer loss; the Qur'anic passage was revealed about this.
TAB:92:6/r8.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء ،   قال :  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «ما مِنْ يَوْمٍ غَرَبَتْ فِيهِ شَمْسُهُ ،   إلاّ وبِجَنْبَيْها مَلَكانِ يُنادِيانِ

TAB:92:6/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:6/r9.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير
TAB:92:6/r9.claim: A report says this passage was revealed about Abū Bakr, who freed vulnerable Muslim women despite his father's advice to free strong men who could defend him, seeking God's reward.
TAB:92:6/r9.anchor: عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزّبير ،   قال :  كان أبو بكر الصدّيق يُعْتِق على الإسلام بمكة ،   فكان يُعْتِق عجائز ونساء

TAB-FULL:v24p461/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r3.claim: He understands belief in al-husna as trusting that God will replace what one spends.
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {وصدق بالحسنى} [الليل: 6] قال: وصدق بالخلف من الله

TAB-FULL:v24p462/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r1.speaker: عكرمة، مجاهد، ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r1.claim: Several reports retain the interpretation that al-husna is God's promised replacement for what is spent.
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، {فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى} [الليل: 6] قال: بالخلف

TAB-FULL:v24p462/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن، الضحاك، ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes al-husna as God's oneness and the testimony that there is no deity but God.
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن، {وصدق بالحسنى} [الليل: 6] قال: بلا إله إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v24p462/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p462/r4.claim: Another reported gloss identifies al-husna with God's promise.

TAB-FULL:v24p465/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r1.claim: Qatadah says the believer trusts God's good promise and acts accordingly.
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r1.anchor: صدق المؤمن بموعود الله الحسن وأشبه هذه الأقوال

TAB-FULL:v24p465/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r2.claim: He prefers belief in God's promised replacement for spending, since the preceding context concerns a giver seeking that replacement; a Prophetic report supports this reading.
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r2.anchor: عني به التصديق بالخلف من الله على نفقته

TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن أبي الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.claim: The Prophet says angels pray each day for God to replace what a spender gives and ruin what a miser withholds; the passage was revealed in connection with this.
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.anchor: اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا، وأعط ممسكا تلفا

TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.claim: A report says the verses were revealed about Abu Bakr, who freed vulnerable women converts; he told his father he sought reward with God rather than strong allies.
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.anchor: إنما أريد، أظنه قال: ما عند الله

TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.claim: When asked whether people should rely on their written destinies, the Prophet commands them to act: each person is made ready for his path, and he recites the two contrasting passages.

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.claim: Several versions say each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written, yet people must act; each is facilitated toward the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.anchor: لا اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن النزال بن سبرة
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.claim: A report says every soul's outcome is written; in response to an Arab's question the Prophet says God guides each person toward good or evil, with these verses cited.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له، فمن يرد الله به خيرا

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن سعد بن عبيدة وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.claim: When asked what work means if everything is decreed, the Prophet says to act because each person is facilitated for the easier or harder path.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر: سنيسره لليسرى، وسنيسره للعسرى

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.claim: Asked whether people act for something already decided or begin something new, the Prophet answers that every worker is made ready for his work.

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن بشير بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.claim: The Prophet says work follows what the pens and decrees have fixed, but people must still act; each is facilitated for the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.anchor: اعملوا، فكل عامل ميسر لعمله الذي خلق له

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:6:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:6:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:6:anmerkung/r1.claim: Al-ḥusnā literally means the best or the most beautiful.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.claim: The first antithesis pairs virtue and vice catalogues with promises of their eschatological outcomes; first-person plural marks these promises as God's speech and authorizes them alongside the oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.anchor: Diese Ankündigungen stehen in der ersten Person Plural, sind also eindeutig als Gottesrede markiert – ein Mittel literarischer Autorisierung

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.claim: The first stanza is symmetrical, with matching behavior-to-consequence sequences and a cross-rhyme produced by vowel variation, as Neuwirth observes.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die symmetrische Binnengliederung des Gesätzes in eine zweimalige Durchführung des Schemas ‚diesseitiges Verhalten – jenseitige Konsequenz’ unterstreicht ein durch Vokalvariation erzielter Kreuzreimeffekt

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.claim: The two halves are linked by paired terms: giving versus stinginess, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 5 und 8 sind durch die Verwendung von Antonymen aufeinander bezogen: ʾaʿtā, „geben“ vs. baḫila, „geizen“, ittaqā, „gottesfürchtig sein“ vs. istaġnā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

TABRISI:92:5-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:92:5-15/r7.claim: Al-husnā can mean God's good promise; another view takes it as Paradise, the reward of those who do good.
TABRISI:92:5-15/r7.anchor: معناه بالعدة الحسنى وهو قول ابن عباس وقتادة وعكرمة

THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.claim: The giver spends wealth in God's way, fears his Lord and avoids His prohibitions, and believes God will replace what he gave.
THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.anchor: فأما من أعطى ماله في سبيل الله واتقى ربه واجتنب محارمه وصدق بالحسنى أي بالخلف

THALABI:v10p216#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p216#3/r8.speaker: عكرمة وشهر بن حوشب عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p216#3/r8.claim: They interpret al-husna as confidence in God's recompense and replacement of what was given.
THALABI:v10p216#3/r8.anchor: وهذه رواية عكرمة وشهر بن حوشب، عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v10p217/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
THALABI:v10p217/r1.claim: At each sunset two angels call out for all creatures except humans and jinn: God should repay the spender and destroy the hoarder; the passage was revealed about this contrast.
THALABI:v10p217/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من يوم غربت شمسه إلا

THALABI:v10p217/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك وعطية عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p217/r2.claim: They interpret al-husna as the declaration 'There is no god but God.'
THALABI:v10p217/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك: وصدق بالحسنى، ب (لا إله إلا الله)

THALABI:v10p217/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p217/r3.claim: He interprets al-husna as Paradise, citing the promise of the best reward and more.
THALABI:v10p217/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بالجنة، ودليله قوله سبحانه للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة

THALABI:v10p217/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r4.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v10p217/r4.claim: They say al-husna is God's promise to reward the believer.
THALABI:v10p217/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي: بموعود الله الذي وعده أن يثيبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p78/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p78/r1.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p78/r1.claim: They explain al-husna as the recompense or return promised by God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p78/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة عن ابن عباس: بالخلف (¬4)، وهو قول الكلبي (¬5)، ومقاتل

WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r1.claim: One interpretation says he believes God will compensate him.
WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r1.anchor: أيقن بأن الله سبحانه سيخلف عليه

WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r2.claim: Another interpretation identifies al-husna with the testimony that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-QT:92:6/r2.anchor: وقيل صدق ب لا اله إلا الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r4.claim: “The best” means certainty God will repay him; another view reads it as belief in God's oneness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r4.anchor: { وصدق بالحسنى } أيقن بأن الله سبحانه سيخلف عليه. وقيل: صدق ب لا إله إلا الله.

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r3.claim: Believing in al-husnā means affirming real goodness, distinguishing virtue from vice, and trusting that good-doers receive better and greater reward, Paradise, and a beautiful final outcome.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r3.anchor: hakikatte bir güzellik ve güzellerin en güzeli bulunduğuna inanmış; iyiyi kötüyü, fazileti rezîleti fark etmiş

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r4.claim: Husnā is the feminine form of the superlative ahsan, used as a noun after its qualified noun is omitted.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r4.anchor: “Hüsnâ” mâlum ki yukarılarda geçtiği üzere “ahsen” ism-i tafdîlinin müennesi, daha güzel veya en güzel mânasına sıfat olduğu hâlde, mevsûfunun hazfiyle isim olarak kullanılmıştır.

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r5.claim: Interpretations of al-husnā include the best trait such as faith or ihsan, the best word such as tawhid or the Qur'an, the best religion of Islam, or the best recompense and Paradise.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r5.anchor: “haslet-i hüsnâ” en güzel haslet: iman ve ihsan hasleti veya “kelime-i hüsnâ” en güzel kelime: kelime-i tevhid

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r6.claim: In context, al-husnā most usefully means the better reward and final outcome promised to those who do good, or the verses promising it.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r6.anchor: siyâka nazaran en zâhir ve en müfid olan mâna ihsan eden, Allah için güzellik yapan muhsinlere ileride daha güzeliyle karşılık

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r7.claim: Practical affirmation matters: one who believes the promise tries sincerely to realize goodness, rather than merely saying the promise is true.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r7.anchor: mücerred doğrudur demek değil, fiilen sadakatle icrâsı dahi matlub

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.claim: Belief in al-husnā precedes giving and taqwa in the order of being, but the text mentions those acts first for two rhetorical reasons.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.anchor: tertîb-i vücûdîde i‘tâ ve ittikāya mukaddemdir. O fazilet ve ihsan, o tasdîke terettüb eder. Böyle iken zikirde i‘tâ ve ittikānın takdim edilmesinde iki nükte vardır.

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.claim: The first reason is that affirmation is required in practice as well as belief and speech: giving and taqwa are primary acts, and verbal belief without them does not earn the promise of ease.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.anchor: fiiliyyâtta hiç eseri zâhir olmayan tasdîke burada zikrolunacak yüsrâ vaadi terettüb etmez.

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.claim: The believer expects the afterlife to be better, remains optimistic about good and pessimistic about evil, and accepts hardship for virtue because it ends in happiness.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.anchor: sonu pek güzel saadet olduğuna, rezîletin önü rahat ve lezzet

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.claim: Because ihsan gives delight, such a person gives gladly, does not begrudge wealth or effort spent on good, and endures sacrifice to avoid evil.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.anchor: i‘tâ ve ittikāyı huzur ve itmi’nân-ı kalb ile seve seve yapar, hayra sarfeylediği mal ve cehde acımaz

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.claim: The second reason for mentioning giving and taqwa first is that effects and recompense follow their causes and deeds; al-husnā is their resulting goal.
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.anchor: müsebbeb sebebden, ivaz mu‘avvazdan, ecr ü mükâfâta istihkak vazife ve amelden muahhar olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r4.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r4.claim: Commentators explain husna as faith, the testimony of God's oneness, Islam, prayer, fasting and almsgiving, or the beautiful reward of worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r4.anchor: müfessirler “iman, kelime-i tevhid, en güzel din olan İslâm, namaz, oruç ve zekât, ibadetlerin güzel karşılığı” gibi anlamlarla açıklamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r5.claim: Here husna best means the whole of Islamic belief and practice, including creed, worship, social dealings, and ethics.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r5.anchor: Bize göre hüsnâ kelimesi bu bağlamda inanç, ibadet, muâmelât ve ahlâk ilkeleriyle İslâm inanç ve uygulamaları bütününü ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s instruction to act rather than rely on one’s recorded destiny, since each is facilitated toward what he was created for; he then recited these verses.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.anchor: عن علي قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - "ما منكم من أحد إلا كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار"

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports that Abū Bakr’s father urged him to free strong slaves who could protect him, but Abū Bakr said he sought another purpose; the verses were revealed concerning him and his father’s advice.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.anchor: محمد بن إسحاق، عن محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي عتيق، عن عامر بن عبد الله، عن بعض أهله، قال أبو قحافة لابنه أبي بكر: يا بني أراك تعتق

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r2.claim: Abū al-Daḥdāḥ represents the giver who fears God, believes in the best reward, and is eased toward Paradise.
THALABI:v10p220/r2.anchor: فأما من أعطى واتقى أبو الدحداح وصدق بالحسنى يعني الثواب فسنيسره لليسرى يعني الجنة

ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r1.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form of al-aḥsan.

ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and others identify al-ḥusnā with God’s sworn promise of reward given in this world.
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة : هي الحلف في الدنيا الوارد به وعد الله تعالى .

ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r3.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r3.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and others identify it as Paradise.

ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r4.speaker: جماعة
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r4.claim: Another group identifies it as reward.

ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r5.speaker: السلمي وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r5.claim: Al-Sulamī and others identify it as the testimony that there is no god but God.
ABUHAYYAN:92:6/r5.anchor: وقال السلمي وغيره : لا إله إلا الله .

ALUSI:92:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
ALUSI:92:6/r1.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and others, with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, identify al-ḥusnā as the best word, there is no god but God.
ALUSI:92:6/r1.anchor: كما قال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وغيره وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس لا إله إلا الله

ALUSI:92:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:92:6/r2.claim: Another view takes al-ḥusnā as whatever signifies truth, centrally including the declaration of divine unity.
ALUSI:92:6/r2.anchor: أو هي ما دلت على حق كما قال بعضهم وتدخل كلمة التوحيد دخولاً أولياً

ALUSI:92:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r3.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI:92:6/r3.claim: ʿIkrima and a group identify al-ḥusnā as the best religion, Islam.
ALUSI:92:6/r3.anchor: وهي ملة الإسلام وقال عكرمة وجماعة

ALUSI:92:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:92:6/r4.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says al-ḥusnā is reward returned in this world with increase.
ALUSI:92:6/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أيضاً هي المثوبة بالخلف في الدنيا مع المضاعفة

ALUSI:92:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r6.claim: Another reported interpretation is reward in general.

ALUSI:92:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r7.claim: Al-Alūsī prefers giving as financial worship, taqwā as all other worship through good acts and avoiding sins, and belief in al-ḥusnā as tawḥīd or comprehensive faith; together they cover all endeavors.
ALUSI:92:6/r7.anchor: ويترجح عندي أن الإعطاء إشارة إلى العبادة المالية والاتفاء إشارة إلى ما يشمل سائر

ALUSI:92:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r11.claim: Faith follows taqwā as a special after a general, and is delayed despite its importance to preserve the verse ending.
ALUSI:92:6/r11.anchor: ولما كان الإيمان أمراً معتنى به في نفسه

ALUSI:92:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r12.claim: One view makes giving obedience, taqwā avoidance of sin, and al-ḥusnā the word of truth such as tawḥīd; al-Alūsī objects that giving conventionally concerns money, especially opposite withholding, and the order remains unexplained.
ALUSI:92:6/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد أعطي الطاعة واتتقي المعصية وصدق بالكلمة الدالة على الحق

ALUSI:92:6/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r13.claim: Another explanation says obedience includes listening to learn tawḥīd and taqwā includes avoiding idolatry, both preceding faith; al-Alūsī rejects it.
ALUSI:92:6/r13.anchor: وقيل آخر لأن من جملة إعطاء الطاعة الإصغاء لتعلم كلمة التوحيد

ALUSI:92:10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI:92:10/r5.claim: Al-Irshād says giving and withholding head the two clauses, though lower in rank than what follows, because each is foundational to the ensuing faith and piety or denial and self-sufficiency.
ALUSI:92:10/r5.anchor: لعل تصدير القسمين بالإعطاء والبخل مع أن كلا منهما أدنى رتبة مما بعد

BAGHAWI:92:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:6/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن والضحاك
BAGHAWI:92:6/r1.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman and al-Dahhak explain al-husna as the testimony that there is no god but God; this is also Atiyya's report from Ibn Abbas.
BAGHAWI:92:6/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن والضحاك : وصدق بلا إله إلا الله

BAGHAWI:92:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:6/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI:92:6/r2.claim: Mujahid says al-husna means Paradise, supported by the verse promising al-husna to those who do good.
BAGHAWI:92:6/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد : بالجنة ،   دليله : قوله تعالى

BAGHAWI:92:6/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:6/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI:92:6/r3.claim: Another view takes al-husna as God's replacement or recompense, trusted to be provided; this is Ikrima's report from Ibn Abbas.
BAGHAWI:92:6/r3.anchor: وقيل { صدق بالحسنى } : أي بالخلف ،   أي أيقن أن الله تعالى سيخلفه

BAGHAWI:92:6/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:6/r4.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI:92:6/r4.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi interpret it as believing God's promise, which God will fulfill.
BAGHAWI:92:6/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي : بموعود الله عز وجل الذي وعده أن يفي به

BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.claim: An anonymous report says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a garment and ten coins and freeing him; their opposed efforts are contrasted.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.anchor: قيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية ابن خلف ببردة وعشرة أوراق ،   فأعتقه

BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.claim: Ata recounts an Ansari's palm tree whose fallen dates entered a neighbor's home; the Prophet offered a tree in Paradise, the owner refused, and Abu al-Dahdah bought it with his garden and gave it to the neighbor. The report maps the giver to Abu al-Dahdah and the miser to the Ansari.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.anchor: عن عطاء ،   قال : " كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة وكان له جار يسقط من بلحها في داره

BAYDAWI:92:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:6/r1.claim: Al-ḥusnā is a beautiful statement conveying truth, such as the declaration of God's oneness.
BAYDAWI:92:6/r1.anchor: وصدق بالكلمة الحسنى وهي ما دلت على حق ككلمة التوحيد

BIQAI:92:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:6/r1.claim: To affirm is to make the informant's statement true through one's assent.

BIQAI:92:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:6/r2.claim: “The best” is the word of justice: the most beautiful speech, namely monotheism and its implications, including true afterlife promises, God's replacement for worldly spending, Islam's eventual dominance despite few adherents, and all the Messenger's promises from God.
BIQAI:92:6/r2.anchor: كلمة العدل التي هي أحسن الكلام من التوحيد وما يتفرع عنه

DURR:92:4/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:4/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR:92:4/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal, and that the revelation contrasts Abu Bakr's effort with that of Umayya and Ubayy, identifying faith in the good as monotheism and the hard outcome as Hell.
DURR:92:4/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أن أبا بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية بن خلف وأبي بن خلف ببردة وعشر أواق

DURR:92:5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r2.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the person affirms God's recompense, and God makes the person easy for good.
DURR:92:5/r2.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى } من الفضل { واتقى } قال : اتقى ربه

DURR:92:5/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī

IBNATIYYA:92:6/r1.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and others identify al-ḥusnā as the declaration that there is no god but God.
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r1.anchor: فقال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وغيره : هي لا إله إلا الله

IBNATIYYA:92:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and others identify al-ḥusnā as the recompense God promised.
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة : هي الخلف الذي وعد الله تعالى به

IBNATIYYA:92:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r3.claim: The cited two-angel hadith has one angel pray that a giver receive recompense and the other that a miser suffer loss; no grading is stated in the commentary.
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r3.anchor: وذلك نص في حديث الملكين إذ يقول أحدهما : اللهم اعط منفقاً خلفاً

IBNATIYYA:92:6/r4.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and others take al-ḥusnā to mean Paradise.
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن وجماعة : { الحسنى } : الجنة

IBNATIYYA:92:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r5.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r5.claim: Many commentators take al-ḥusnā to mean reward and recompense in general.
IBNATIYYA:92:6/r5.anchor: وقال كثير من المفسرين { الحسنى } : الأجر والثواب مجملاً

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r1.claim: Qatada understands al-ḥusnā as recompense for the giving and piety just mentioned.

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r2.speaker: خصيف
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r2.claim: Khasif interprets al-ḥusnā as the reward.
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r2.anchor: على ذلك - قاله قتادة ،   وقال خصيف : بالثواب

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وأبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r3.claim: These authorities interpret al-ḥusnā as replacement or compensation.
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ،   ومجاهد ،   وعكرمة ،   وأبو صالح ،   وزيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r4.claim: Al-Sulami and al-Dahhak interpret al-ḥusnā as the testimony lā ilāha illā Allāh.
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي ،   والضحاك

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r5.claim: In one narration from ʿIkrima, al-ḥusnā means what God bestowed upon the person.
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r5.anchor: وفي رواية عن عكرمة : { وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى } أي : بما أنعم الله عليه

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r6.claim: In one narration Zayd ibn Aslam interprets al-ḥusnā as prayer, alms, and fasting.
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r6.anchor: وفي رواية عن زيد بن أسلم : { وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى } قال : الصلاة والزكاة والصوم

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam also gave the interpretation of the obligatory charity at the end of Ramadan.
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r7.anchor: وفي رواية عن زيد بن أسلم : { وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى } قال : الصلاة والزكاة والصوم .   وقال مرة : وصدقة الفطر

IBNKATHIR:92:6/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r8.claim: Asked by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb about al-ḥusnā, the Prophet answered that it is Paradise; Ibn Kathir gives no grading here.
IBNKATHIR:92:6/r8.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الحسنى قال : " الحسنى : الجنة "

MAWARDI:92:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:6/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:92:6/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses al-ḥusnā as God's oneness, expressed in the testimony There is no god but God.
MAWARDI:92:6/r1.anchor: أحدها : بتوحيد الله ،   وهو قول لا إله إلا الله ،   قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI:92:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:6/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:92:6/r2.claim: Qatāda takes it as what God has promised.

MAWARDI:92:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:6/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI:92:6/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam takes it as prayer, alms, and fasting.
MAWARDI:92:6/r5.anchor: الخامس : بالصلاة والزكاة والصوم ،   قاله زيد بن أسلم

MAWARDI:92:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:6/r6.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI:92:6/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets it as believing what God has bestowed upon him.
MAWARDI:92:6/r6.anchor: السادس : بما أنعم الله عليه ،   قاله عطاء

MAWARDI:92:6/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:6/r7.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:92:6/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes it as trusting that God will replace what one gives; Māwardī notes that most of these glosses are close in meaning.
MAWARDI:92:6/r7.anchor: السابع : بالخلف من عطائه ،   قاله الحسن ،   ومعاني أكثرها متقاربة

NASAFI:92:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:6/r1.claim: Al-ḥusnā may mean the most beautiful religion, Islam.
NASAFI:92:6/r1.anchor: { وَصَدَّقَ بالحسنى } بالملة الحسنى وهي ملة الإسلام

NASAFI:92:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:6/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is the finest reward, Paradise.

NASAFI:92:6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:6/r3.claim: Or it is the excellent declaration “There is no god but God.”
NASAFI:92:6/r3.anchor: أو بالكلمة الحسنى وهي لا إله إلا الله

QURTUBI:92:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:6/r1.claim: He explains believing in the good as trusting that God will repay what one gives.
QURTUBI:92:6/r1.anchor: أي بالخلف من اللّه تعالى على عطائه

QURTUBI:92:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
QURTUBI:92:6/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that two angels descend each morning, one asking God to recompense the spender and the other to ruin the miser.
QURTUBI:92:6/r2.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم : ( ما من يوم يصبح العباد فيه إلا

QURTUBI:92:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
QURTUBI:92:6/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that at sunset two angels call for recompense for the spender and loss for the miser; the passage was revealed in connection with this.
QURTUBI:92:6/r3.anchor: وروى من حديث أبي الدرداء : أن رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من يوم غربت شمسه إلا بعث

QURTUBI:92:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r7.speaker: الضحاك والسلمي وابن عباس
QURTUBI:92:6/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak, al-Sulami, and Ibn Abbas interpret the good as the testimony that there is no god but God.
QURTUBI:92:6/r7.anchor: قاله الضحاك والسلمي وابن عباس أيضا

QURTUBI:92:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:92:6/r8.claim: Mujahid interprets the good as Paradise, citing the promise of the best reward and more.
QURTUBI:92:6/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد : بالجنة . دليله قوله تعالى

QURTUBI:92:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:92:6/r9.claim: Qatada says it means believing God's promise to reward him.
QURTUBI:92:6/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة : بموعود اللّه الذي وعده أن يثيبه

QURTUBI:92:6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r10.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI:92:6/r10.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets it as believing in prayer, almsgiving, and fasting.
QURTUBI:92:6/r10.anchor: زيد بن أسلم : بالصلاة والزكاة والصوم

QURTUBI:92:6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:92:6/r11.claim: Al-Hasan takes it as trusting that God will repay his giving; al-Tabari prefers this interpretation.
QURTUBI:92:6/r11.anchor: الحسن : بالخلف من عطائه ، وهو اختيار الطبري

QURTUBI:92:6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:6/r12.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the interpretations are close because they all return to reward, which is Paradise.
QURTUBI:92:6/r12.anchor: إذ كله يرجع إلى الثواب الذي هو الجنة

RAZI:92:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:1/r2.claim: Despite that reported occasion, the sūra’s meaning is general, as its statements that human striving differs and that a blazing fire is warned of show.
RAZI:92:1/r2.anchor: إلا أنها وإن كانت كذلك لكن معانيها عامة للناس

RAZI:92:1/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:1/r3.speaker: علي
RAZI:92:1/r3.claim: ʿAlī reports that at a funeral the Prophet said God knows every soul’s place in Paradise or Hell; when asked whether to rely on this, he said to act, since each is facilitated for what they were created for.
RAZI:92:1/r3.anchor: ويروى عن علي عليه السلام أنه قال : «خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI:92:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:5/r1.claim: The paired descriptions explain how differing deeds lead to good or bad outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI:92:5/r1.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة

RAZI:92:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:6/r1.claim: One interpretation is lā ilāha illā Allāh: giving and avoiding prohibitions do not benefit without faith in divine unity and prophecy.
RAZI:92:6/r1.anchor: أنها قول لا إله إلا الله

RAZI:92:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:6/r2.claim: Another interpretation is the good in God’s prescribed bodily and financial acts of worship: one gives for God, avoids prohibitions, and affirms the laws’ beneficial purposes.
RAZI:92:6/r2.anchor: أن الحسنى عبارة عما فرضه الله تعالى من العبادات

RAZI:92:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:92:6/r3.claim: A third interpretation is God’s promised replacement for spending; the giver trusts that promise, and the replacement exceeds what was spent.
RAZI:92:6/r3.anchor: أن الحسنى هو الخلف الذي وعده الله في قوله

RAZI:92:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r4.speaker: أبي الدرداء
RAZI:92:6/r4.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports that two angels call each sunset for all creation except humans and jinn: God, replace what the spender gave and bring loss to the one who withholds.
RAZI:92:6/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي الدرداء أنه قال : «ما من يوم غربت فيه الشمس

RAZI:92:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:92:6/r6.claim: A fourth interpretation is the reward, or Paradise; the two explanations amount to the same thing.

RAZI:92:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r7.speaker: قتادة
RAZI:92:6/r7.claim: Qatāda says the person believed God’s promise and acted for that reward.
RAZI:92:6/r7.anchor: قال قتادة : صدق بموعود الله فعمل لذلك الموعود

RAZI:92:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r8.speaker: القفال
RAZI:92:6/r8.claim: Al-Qaffāl says al-ḥusnā encompasses every good quality, as verses use it for good outcomes, increased reward, and good recompense.
RAZI:92:6/r8.anchor: قال القفال : وبالجملة أن الحسنى لفظة تسع كل خصلة حسنة
